assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites turned a simple solution-processable crystalline framework into a photovoltaic absorber with efficiencies rivalling silicon in about a decade. The structure-property story (defect tolerance, long carrier lifetimes, compositional tunability of the ABX3 lattice) is a textbook case of designed inorganic architecture giving a new function with clear application relevance.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka's 2009 dye-sensitized-cell work first used the perovskite as a light absorber; Snaith and Park/Gratzel's solid-state devices around 2012 made the efficiency step change. Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis are also decisive, so a three-person limit forces a contested cut. I would propose Miyasaka, Snaith and Park, but the allocation is genuinely unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency and device confirmation are extensive and independent, and tandem and commercial development are advancing. Operational stability, lead content and degradation mechanisms are still open, so timing is arguably slightly early but defensible.
uncertainties: Long-term stability and toxicity may weaken the case for a prize now.
Credit among Miyasaka, Snaith, Park, Gratzel, Seok and Kanatzidis is contested; I rely on recalled history, not verification.
Whether the committee sees this as materials/physics rather than chemistry.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational design of zeolites and related molecular sieves with controlled pore architecture and active sites underpins refining, petrochemicals and emissions control at enormous industrial scale. Organic structure-directing agents, new framework topologies and site-isolated catalysis connect atomic structure to selectivity directly. This is a field I know well, so I discount for possible bias.
assessment.attribution: Corma (catalyst design, tailored frameworks), Davis (templating, new large-pore materials, catalysis) and Zones (SDA-based synthesis, Chevron SSZ materials) are central, while Yu and Tsapatsis are also important. The category is broad and Barrer/Breck-era pioneers are absent, so the credited set is a fair but not obviously unique trio.
assessment.maturity: Decades of independent validation and industrial deployment; recognition is not premature, and some may argue it is overdue. Structure determination of new zeolites increasingly relies on electron diffraction and microED-type methods, which strengthens confirmation of the claimed architectures.
uncertainties: Discovery is a field rather than a single event, making a crisp prize citation hard.
Possible conflict of interest given my own zeolite research; I should be cautious in committee debate.
Corma's recent death status and priority claims among the named people are not verified by me.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Base editors install precise point mutations without double-strand breaks by coupling engineered deaminases to a programmable Cas9 nickase, creating a chemistry-led genome-editing modality that is already in clinical trials. The protein-engineering and directed-evolution component is rigorous and the impact on therapeutics is substantial.
assessment.attribution: Liu's laboratory made the decisive cytosine and adenine base editors, with Komor and Gaudelli the lead first authors; Nishida and Kondo independently reported a related Target-AID system. Liu may be the core laureate, but a three-person slate including the trainees is unusual, and Liu also has strong prime-editing claims in B061.
assessment.maturity: Rapid, reproducible adoption across many labs and first clinical outcomes, though long-term safety and off-target deamination are still being assessed. Maturity is adequate but the prize may arrive via a broader CRISPR-genome-editing framing.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize and with prime editing (B061) complicates the citation.
Independent priority of Target-AID is not resolved.
Long-term clinical safety data are limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation, through bifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues, reprogrammed the ubiquitin-proteasome system to eliminate proteins previously considered undruggable. The concept is original, chemically well defined and has opened a new pharmacological class with many clinical candidates.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies introduced the PROTAC concept, Ciulli delivered structure-guided VHL ligands and ternary-complex understanding, and Handa/Ito's work on thalidomide-cereblon is a separate but essential molecular-glue thread. The credit split between PROTAC and glue branches is unresolved and a three-person set leaves out important contributors.
assessment.maturity: Strong mechanistic and structural support (ternary complex structures, cereblon identification) and many clinical programs; approved drugs are still lacking, so clinical validation is not yet complete.
uncertainties: No approved degrader yet, so real-world impact is still pending.
Compound discovery: PROTACs and molecular glues may need different recognition.
Attribution of cereblon mechanism to Handa/Ito versus the PROTAC pioneers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative mass-spectrometry proteomics made it possible to identify and measure thousands of proteins and their modifications in cells, transforming biochemistry and medicine. The methods are enabling in the sense I value, letting a whole community see what it could not before.
assessment.attribution: Mann (high-resolution, SILAC and proteome-scale workflows), Aebersold (targeted and SRM/SWATH, ICAT) and Yates (shotgun/MudPIT, database search) each made distinct and decisive contributions; Gygi, Heck and Hunt are also strong, so the cut is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Very mature, widely confirmed and routinely used; an earlier mass-spectrometry prize (2002) covered ionization, so a proteomics-focused award is plausible but may be seen as overlapping with native MS and Orbitrap.
uncertainties: Overlap with B031 native MS and B050 Orbitrap in any combined analytical-MS citation.
Large number of equally deserving contributors.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Determining the structure of nitrogenase, including the FeMo-cofactor with its interstitial carbide, gave the atomic basis for biological nitrogen fixation, one of the central problems in bioinorganic chemistry. Crystallographic evidence is concrete and the work directly addresses the mechanism of a globally important reaction.
assessment.attribution: Rees solved the first structures and the cofactor environment, Einsle located the central light atom at high resolution, and Dean's genetics and biochemistry established the system; Seefeldt and Ribbe contributed key mechanistic and cofactor work. Allocation is plausible but the mechanistic picture belongs to a wider group.
assessment.maturity: Structures are well replicated, but the catalytic mechanism (substrate binding, E4 intermediate, hydride chemistry) is still evolving, so the recognised discovery would be primarily structural; timing is reasonable though mechanism is incomplete.
uncertainties: Catalytic mechanism is not fully settled.
Credit between structural and biochemical contributors is open.
I recall but have not verified the identification of the interstitial carbide.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Single-atom catalysis extends the idea of maximal atom efficiency to isolated metal atoms on supports, with demonstrated activity and selectivity in several reactions and wide uptake across catalysis and energy research. The conceptual framing is attractive and the materials-design relevance is high.
assessment.attribution: Zhang, Qiao and Liu are linked to the 2011 Pt1/FeOx work that popularised the term, with Wang and Li as co-authors and earlier related ideas by others; priority for the concept versus the demonstrated systems is not clean, and the credit set is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Confirmation by aberration-corrected STEM and XAS is extensive but active-site identity, dynamics under reaction conditions and stability remain debated; recognition may be somewhat premature.
uncertainties: Structural proof of truly isolated active sites under operating conditions is often incomplete.
Concept priority overlaps with earlier supported-metal catalysis.
Industrial impact is still limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Serial femtosecond crystallography at X-ray free-electron lasers enables structure determination from micro- and nanocrystals and time-resolved studies of reactions, in the spirit of crystallography without large crystals. It is a genuine enabling method, closely related in concept to my own electron-crystallography interests.
assessment.attribution: Chapman led the proof-of-principle and diffraction-before-destruction concept, Fromme contributed crystal and sample strategies, and Schlichting contributed time-resolved applications; Hajdu is credited but I am not certain of his current status. Credit is spread across many people and facilities.
assessment.maturity: Method has been reproduced on several XFELs and has produced time-resolved structures, but a landmark chemical discovery is less clear than the technique, and impact is smaller than long-established structural methods.
uncertainties: Biological structural results from SFX remain modest relative to synchrotron and cryo-EM.
Allocation among many participants is unresolved.
May be considered more physics or structural biology than chemistry.
